passages.text: Ephraim chases the wind and pursues the east wind all day long; he multiplies lies and violence; he makes a covenant with Assyria and sends olive oil to Egypt.
passages.sermon:
Ephraim is a tribe in Israel.
Ephraim chases the wind.
Ephraim runs after the east wind all day.
Ephraim increases lies.
Ephraim increases violence.
Ephraim makes a covenant with Assyria.
Ephraim sends olive oil to Egypt.
passages.original: אֶפְרַ֜יִם רֹעֶ֥ה ר֙וּחַ֙ וְרֹדֵ֣ף קָדִ֔ים כָּל־ הַיּ֕וֹם כָּזָ֥ב וָשֹׁ֖ד יַרְבֶּ֑ה וּבְרִית֙ עִם־ אַשּׁ֣וּר יִכְרֹ֔תוּ וְשֶׁ֖מֶן לְמִצְרַ֥יִם יוּבָֽל׃

passages.text: The LORD also brings a charge against Judah. He will punish Jacob according to his ways and repay him according to his deeds.
passages.sermon:
The LORD brings a charge against Judah.
The LORD accuses Judah of wrongdoing.
The LORD will punish Jacob for his actions.
The LORD will repay Jacob for what he has done.
The LORD judges each person by their deeds.
The LORD gives to each one what they deserve.
passages.original: וְרִ֥יב לַֽיהוָ֖ה עִם־ יְהוּדָ֑ה וְלִפְקֹ֤ד עַֽל־ יַעֲקֹב֙ כִּדְרָכָ֔יו כְּמַעֲלָלָ֖יו יָשִׁ֥יב לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: In the womb he grasped his brother’s heel, and in his vigor he wrestled with God.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was a man.
Jacob had a brother.
Jacob grasped his brother’s heel while he was still in the womb.
Jacob was strong.
Jacob wrestled with God using his strength.
passages.original: בַּבֶּ֖טֶן עָקַ֣ב אֶת־ אָחִ֑יו וּבְאוֹנ֖וֹ שָׂרָ֥ה אֶת־ אֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: Yes, he struggled with the angel and prevailed; he wept and sought His favor; he found Him at Bethel and spoke with Him there — the LORD is the God of Hosts— the LORD is His name of renown.
passages.sermon:
Jacob struggled with the angel.
Jacob prevailed over the angel.
Jacob wept.
Jacob begged the angel for favor.
Jacob found God at Bethel.
God spoke with us at Bethel.
The LORD is the God of Hosts.
The LORD is His famous name.
passages.original: וָיָּ֤שַׂר אֶל־ מַלְאָךְ֙ וַיֻּכָ֔ל בָּכָ֖ה וַיִּתְחַנֶּן־ ל֑וֹ בֵּֽית־ אֵל֙ יִמְצָאֶ֔נּוּ וְשָׁ֖ם יְדַבֵּ֥ר עִמָּֽנוּ׃ וַֽיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י הַצְּבָא֑וֹת יְהוָ֖ה זִכְרֽוֹ׃

passages.text: But you must return to your God, maintaining love and justice, and always waiting on your God.
passages.sermon:
You must return to your God.
You must keep love.
You must keep justice.
You must always wait for your God.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֖ה בֵּאלֹהֶ֣יךָ תָשׁ֑וּב חֶ֤סֶד וּמִשְׁפָּט֙ שְׁמֹ֔ר וְקַוֵּ֥ה אֶל־ אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ תָּמִֽיד׃

passages.text: A merchant loves to defraud with dishonest scales in his hands.
passages.sermon:
A merchant uses dishonest scales.
He holds these scales in his hands.
He loves to cheat others.
He loves to defraud people.
passages.original: כְּנַ֗עַן בְּיָד֛וֹ מֹאזְנֵ֥י מִרְמָ֖ה לַעֲשֹׁ֥ק אָהֵֽב׃

passages.text: And Ephraim boasts: “How rich I have become! I have found wealth for myself. In all my labors, they can find in me no iniquity that is sinful.”
passages.sermon:
Ephraim is a tribe in Israel.
Ephraim speaks with pride.
Ephraim says, "I have become rich."
Ephraim says, "I have found wealth for myself."
Ephraim says, "In all my work, no one can find guilt in me."
Ephraim says, "No one can find sin in what I have done."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶפְרַ֔יִם אַ֣ךְ עָשַׁ֔רְתִּי מָצָ֥אתִי א֖וֹן לִ֑י כָּל־ יְגִיעַ֕י לֹ֥א יִמְצְאוּ־ לִ֖י עָוֺ֥ן אֲשֶׁר־ חֵֽטְא׃

passages.text: But I am the LORD your God ever since the land of Egypt. I will again make you dwell in tents, as in the days of the appointed feast.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your God.
He brought you out of the land of Egypt.
He has always been your God since that time.
He will make you live in tents again.
You will dwell in tents as you did during the days of the appointed feast.
passages.original: וְאָנֹכִ֛י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם עֹ֛ד אוֹשִֽׁיבְךָ֥ בָאֳהָלִ֖ים כִּימֵ֥י מוֹעֵֽד׃

passages.text: I spoke through the prophets and multiplied their visions; I gave parables through the prophets.
passages.sermon:
God is the speaker.
God spoke through the prophets.
God gave many visions to the prophets.
God used the prophets to give parables.
passages.original: וְדִבַּ֙רְתִּי֙ עַל־ הַנְּבִיאִ֔ים וְאָנֹכִ֖י חָז֣וֹן הִרְבֵּ֑יתִי וּבְיַ֥ד הַנְּבִיאִ֖ים אֲדַמֶּֽה׃

passages.text: Is there iniquity in Gilead? They will surely come to nothing. Do they sacrifice bulls in Gilgal? Indeed, their altars will be heaps of stones in the furrows of the field.
passages.sermon:
Gilead is a place in Israel.
Gilead is full of iniquity.
Gilead will come to nothing.
Gilgal is another place in Israel.
The people in Gilgal sacrifice bulls.
Their altars will become heaps of stones.
These heaps will lie in the furrows of the field.
passages.original: אִם־ גִּלְעָ֥ד אָ֙וֶן֙ אַךְ־ שָׁ֣וְא הָי֔וּ בַּגִּלְגָּ֖ל שְׁוָרִ֣ים זִבֵּ֑חוּ גַּ֤ם מִזְבְּחוֹתָם֙ כְּגַלִּ֔ים עַ֖ל תַּלְמֵ֥י שָׂדָֽי׃

passages.text: Jacob fled to the land of Aram and Israel worked for a wife— for a wife he tended sheep.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was a patriarch of Israel.
Jacob fled to the land of Aram.
Jacob left his home because he was in danger.
Jacob worked to obtain a wife.
Jacob tended sheep for a wife.
Jacob served faithfully for this purpose.
passages.original: וַיִּבְרַ֥ח יַעֲקֹ֖ב שְׂדֵ֣ה אֲרָ֑ם וַיַּעֲבֹ֤ד יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּאִשָּׁ֔ה וּבְאִשָּׁ֖ה שָׁמָֽר׃

passages.text: But by a prophet the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt, and by a prophet he was preserved.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD used a prophet.
The LORD brought Israel out of Egypt by a prophet.
The LORD kept Israel safe by a prophet.
passages.original: וּבְנָבִ֕יא הֶעֱלָ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וּבְנָבִ֖יא נִשְׁמָֽר׃

passages.text: Ephraim has provoked bitter anger, so his Lord will leave his bloodguilt upon him and repay him for his contempt.
passages.sermon:
Ephraim is a tribe in Israel.
Ephraim has made God very angry.
Ephraim has caused bitter anger.
The Lord is Ephraim’s master.
The Lord will not remove Ephraim’s guilt for bloodshed.
The Lord will let Ephraim bear his own guilt.
The Lord will repay Ephraim for his contempt.
The Lord will give Ephraim what he deserves for his shameful actions.
passages.original: הִכְעִ֥יס אֶפְרַ֖יִם תַּמְרוּרִ֑ים וְדָמָיו֙ עָלָ֣יו יִטּ֔וֹשׁ וְחֶ֨רְפָּת֔וֹ יָשִׁ֥יב ל֖וֹ אֲדֹנָֽיו׃
